pages.title: DMC Rengine — DMC3 HD Reverse Engineering
pages.description: Evidence-backed C++20 reverse engineering, decompilation research, DMC3 HD file-format documentation and safe modding infrastructure.
pages.summary: DMC Rengine researches Devil May Cry 3: Special Edition from the HD Collection through executable evidence, binary formats, resource materialization, guarded authoring and long-term recompilation work.

sections.heading: Research surface
items: Executable and runtime research ties reverse-engineering claims to concrete artifacts and evidence instead of treating decompiler output or naming guesses as final truth.
File-format work covers scene, model, structural, texture and archive families, with unknown or unresolved fields kept distinct from promoted semantics.
GDSpaces connects numbered archives, containers, slots and resources into a provenance-aware materialization path used by the wider project.

sections.heading: How to use this site
items: Start with the format index when you know a file extension or archive family and need the relevant DMC3 HD research entry point.
Use Current Status before relying on a reader, writer, reintegration path or runtime claim; maturity belongs to the live canonical status rather than these landing pages.
Follow the Canonical source link on every page for exact schemas, evidence records, implementation details and unsupported boundaries.

pages.title: DMC3 HD File Formats — DMC Rengine
pages.description: DMC3 HD format and archive research for SCM, MOD, SHW, HITS, PAC, PNST, NBZ, DDS and PTX.
pages.summary: Browse public entry points for DMC3 HD resource families. Exact schemas, evidence status and current product support remain in canonical GitHub documentation.

sections.heading: Resource families
items: Scene and model research includes SCM, MOD and SHW entry points, separating structural parsing from higher-level runtime or authoring semantics.
Container research includes PAC, PNST and numbered NBZ archives, with slot identity, nesting and materialization treated separately from game-side selection behavior.
Dedicated public entry points now also cover the HITS collision structure and the bounded DDS/PTX texture research surface without flattening those families into one universal format model.

sections.heading: Evidence model
items: A recognizable header or successful parse is not treated as proof that every field has a known semantic meaning.
Unknown bytes and unresolved relationships are preserved or explicitly bounded instead of being assigned convenient names for presentation.
Reader, writer and reintegration maturity changes over time, so this index routes support questions back to Current Status and the canonical format documents.

sections.heading: What SCM research covers
items: SCM is studied as a scene-oriented binary format containing relationships between scene nodes, objects, meshes, vertex streams, transforms and texture-facing state.
Topology reconstruction and runtime-facing fields are kept tied to corpus or executable evidence rather than inferred only from visual output.
Authoring and rebuild work is intentionally bounded: a structurally writable file does not by itself prove equivalence with Capcom tooling or acceptance by every game path.

pages.title: DMC3 HITS Collision Format — DMC Rengine
pages.description: DMC3 HITS collision-format structure, spatial-grid and triangle-plane reverse-engineering entry point.
pages.summary: Entry point for the DMC3 HITS collision resource: header-driven spatial grids, cell references and fixed triangle-plane records, with raw flag semantics and original-game authoring acceptance kept evidence-gated.

sections.heading: What HITS research covers
items: Canonical HITS recognition uses the four-byte HITS magic and a bounded header describing collision-space bounds, cell dimensions, grid counts, the spatial table and the triangle array.
The spatial structure is a three-dimensional acceleration grid whose cells reference lists of triangle byte offsets, so the resource is not modeled as a flat scan of anonymous fixed-size records.
Each structural triangle record preserves raw flags together with three points, a normal and plane value; exact flag meanings remain separate evidence questions rather than presentation-time guesses.

sections.heading: Evidence and compatibility boundaries
items: The obsolete HITS$ interpretation and the idea that 0x18060001 is a universal record marker are explicitly rejected by the current canonical format authority.
Collision purpose and structural parsing are stronger claims than material classes, gameplay responses or traversal semantics, which require direct evidence from the relevant runtime consumers.
A DMC Rengine writer or spatial reconstruction test does not by itself prove that topology-changing output is accepted by every original-game path or equivalent to an external Capcom builder.

pages.title: DMC3 DDS and PTX Textures — DMC Rengine
pages.description: DMC3 DDS and PTX texture-format recognition, framing and resource-representation research.
pages.summary: Entry point for DMC3 texture research across DDS and PTX representations. It keeps bundle framing, wrapped or extracted DDS bytes and runtime texture identity distinct while delegating exact operation maturity to canonical status.

sections.heading: What DDS and PTX research covers
items: DDS is treated as a recognizable HD texture representation with its own compression and layout variants, while PTX is a separate texture bundle or container-like resource surface that can expose texture children.

DMC Rengine keeps runtime-original PTX or TIM2 representations, DDS-bearing container representations, extracted DDS bytes and runtime GPU textures as distinct identities instead of collapsing them into one generic texture object.
Format recognition and Native Reader visibility answer narrower questions than texel editing, conversion, production authoring or reintegration, each of which requires its own validated contract.

sections.heading: Questions this entry point helps answer
items: When is a payload structurally a PTX texture bundle, a descriptor-plus-DDS texture slot or a directly recognizable DDS resource, and which evidence establishes that distinction?
How do texture resources relate to model-facing texture references without assuming that a MOD texture slot, companion entry, internal image and extracted DDS are interchangeable identifiers?

sections.heading: What PAC research covers
items: PAC is treated as a slot-bearing container where physical ordering, sparse or empty entries and payload identity must survive inspection rather than being normalized away for convenience.
Relative offsets and slot relationships are part of the container contract, while resource semantics belong to the nested payload and its own evidence-aware parser.
Reintegration work is guarded so preserving container identity is not confused with proving that every modified nested resource is behaviorally valid in the original game.

Extraction or reconstruction must preserve container-level identity before higher-level tooling can safely reason about the resources materialized from those slots.

Physical archive membership, extracted or materialized coordinate spaces, overlay behavior and runtime resolver decisions are modeled as related but distinct concerns.
A synthetic archive rebuild can prove structural properties without proving which archive or member the original executable will select in every runtime context.

pages.title: GDSpaces — DMC Rengine Resource Architecture
pages.description: DMC Rengine GDSpaces resource resolution, materialization and provenance architecture.
pages.summary: Entry point into the canonical GDSpaces resource resolver/materializer/provenance architecture. The site does not recreate its contracts or state.

sections.heading: What GDSpaces connects
items: GDSpaces is the resource architecture that carries provenance from archive source through member, container and slot layers toward a classified resource instead of flattening those steps into one extraction operation.
Resolver, classifier, container expansion and resource-graph responsibilities are separated so a guessed filename or extension cannot silently override stronger structural evidence.
The architecture lets Stage Ops, readers and future authoring workflows reuse one canonical materialization path instead of embedding format-specific extraction logic in each UI.

pages.title: DMC3 Reverse Engineering — DMC Rengine
pages.description: Evidence-first DMC3 executable, runtime and binary-format reverse-engineering research.
pages.summary: Entry point into evidence-first DMC3 reverse engineering. Exact artifact, address, range and confidence boundaries remain in canonical evidence sources.

sections.heading: Evidence-first reverse engineering
items: DMC Rengine binds strong runtime claims to a canonical executable artifact, machine-code locations or reproducible corpus evidence instead of promoting decompiler names as facts.

Executable confirmation, corpus confirmation, structural confirmation and unresolved candidates are kept distinguishable so later findings can strengthen or reject earlier hypotheses without rewriting history.
Format parsers and runtime analysis cross-check one another: a field that exists in bytes and a field that affects game behavior are related questions, not automatically the same proof.

sections.heading: Questions this entry point helps answer
items: What evidence is required before a guessed format field or runtime relationship becomes a canonical public claim?
How are artifact identity, addresses, byte ranges, corpus samples and evidence status recorded so another researcher can reproduce the result?
How does the project handle contradictory findings, preserved unknowns and hypotheses that fail later executable or corpus checks?

pages.title: DMC Rengine Current Status
pages.description: Current canonical implementation and proof status for DMC Rengine.
pages.summary: Direct entry point to the live project-status authority for promoted capabilities, proof gates and explicit incomplete boundaries.

sections.heading: Why Current Status is authoritative
items: DMC Rengine changes quickly, so support and completion claims are centralized in one live status document instead of being copied into every format landing page or README section.
Promotion separates implemented code from stronger claims such as validated authoring, original-game runtime acceptance or whole-layer completion.
Open blockers and explicit incomplete boundaries remain visible so public discovery pages cannot make experimental work appear production-ready through omission.

sections.heading: Use this page before citing capabilities
items: Check whether a format is currently promoted for structural reading, writing, reintegration or another narrower capability rather than assuming support from its presence in the repository.
Check the active L1, L2 and L3 proof gates when a claim depends on resource materialization, runtime resolution or higher-level tooling behavior.
Use linked canonical evidence and implementation records for exact proof; this discovery page only explains why the live status document is the authority.
